A QRDX node speaks three protocols on one host, and they always agree because they read through the same views:

| | Use it for | Testnet |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **JSON-RPC** | Ethereum-compatible calls, and every QRDX read and write | `POST https://test.qrdx.org/rpc` |
| **REST** | the same data over plain `GET`s, easy from any language | `https://test.qrdx.org/get_…` |
| **Streams** | live blocks, books, trades, tickers and accounts | `wss://test.qrdx.org/ws`, `/stream` (SSE) |

Above the node:

- **QRDX Wallet** signs for users: [wallet integration](/docs/build/wallet-integration) and [QRDX Connect](/docs/build/qrdx-connect).
- **The trade API** (`trade.qrdx.org/api/v1-test`) adds pair orientation, USD prices, account summaries and PnL: [trade API](/docs/build/trade-api).
- **Profiles** (`trade.qrdx.org/api/profiles`): verified names and images: [profiles](/docs/build/profiles).

## The examples on these pages run

Every code block with a **Run** button calls the network chosen in its header, from your browser: testnet by default, or a node on your machine. Edit the code and run it again; **⌘/Ctrl + Enter** runs too.

JavaScript examples run in a sandbox (an iframe that cannot reach this page, its storage or its cookies) with these helpers in scope:

| Helper | Does |
| --- | --- |
| `rpc(method, ...params)` | JSON-RPC; returns `result`, throws on an RPC error |
| `rest(path, query?)` | a node REST `GET`; returns `result` |
| `trade(path)` | the trade API for the chosen network |
| `pq.keygen(seed?)` | an ML-DSA-65 key pair with its `address` and `accountId` |
| `pq.sign(message, secretKey, { raw? })`, `pq.verify(message, signature, publicKey, { raw? })` | QRDX-prefixed message signatures, or raw bytes (hex) with `raw: true` |
| `pq.address(publicKey)`, `pq.accountId(address)` | address and account-id derivation |
| `hash.keccak256(x)`, `hash.blake2b256(x)` | hashes of text or `0x` hex |
| `network` | `{ node, rpc, ws, trade, explorer }` |
| `sleep(ms)` | a pause |

`fetch`, `WebSocket` and `console.table` work as usual. Keys made here live only in the sandbox for that run.

## Libraries

There is no official SDK yet. The examples use plain `fetch` and [`@noble/post-quantum`](https://github.com/paulmillr/noble-post-quantum) for ML-DSA-65, the same library QRDX Wallet uses; any FIPS 204 implementation (liboqs, for example) produces compatible signatures.
